list: The 20 m DEM cannot resolve boulders or small scarps; slopes are averaged over the baseline.
Walking speed, suit power and battery are stated assumptions, not a NASA EVA or life-support model.
Comms uses line of sight from a mast on the habitat; mast and antenna heights are assumptions and no relay or orbiter pass is modelled.
Daylight uses geometric sun elevation from Mars24; no refraction, dust opacity or terrain shading.
No live weather, dust or radiation data.
Feasible means feasible under this model, not certified safe.

raw.label: Cruise stage separation
raw.note: About 10 minutes before entry the cruise stage is shed. Time derived from 'about 10 minutes before entry'.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Entry interface and guided entry
raw.note: Reaches the top of the Martian atmosphere at about 19,500 kph (12,100 mph). Small thrusters on the aeroshell adjust lift for guided entry. Ends at peak heating.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Peak heating
raw.note: Peak heating about 75 s after entry; heat shield surface reaches about 1,300 C (2,370 F). The vehicle then decelerates until the parachute deploys.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Parachute deploy (Range Trigger)
raw.note: About 240 s after entry at about 11 km altitude and about 1,512 kph (940 mph). 21.5 m (70.5 ft) parachute. End time derived: heat shield separates 20 s after deployment.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Heat shield separation
raw.note: 20 s after parachute deployment (derived: 240 + 20). Reveals the radar and the cameras. Radar is active from here to touchdown, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Radar acquires the ground
raw.note: After heat shield separation the landing radar is exposed and starts measuring altitude and velocity, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface, and runs until touchdown. Time bounds: heat shield separation (260 s, derived) to back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Terrain-Relative Navigation
raw.note: Lander Vision System compares camera images with an onboard map at about 4.2 to 2.2 km above the ground, locating the vehicle to about 40 m in under 10 s and able to shift touchdown by up to 600 m (2,000 ft). NASA gives altitudes, not clock times, for this step: it is shown only while the altitude is between 4.2 and 2.2 km; the time bounds are heat shield separation (260 s) and back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Back shell and parachute separation
raw.note: About 90 s after heat shield separation (derived: 260 + 90), powered descent vehicle about 2.1 km (1.3 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing (90 s) and Landing Press Kit (2.1 km)

raw.label: Powered descent
raw.note: Begins at about 306 kph (190 mph) and 2.1 km (6,900 ft); slows to about 2.7 kph (1.7 mph) at about 20 m (66 ft). End bound is touchdown at about 420 s ('EDL ends about seven minutes later'); NASA gives the end as an altitude.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Sky crane
raw.note: Starts when the descent stage is 20 m (65 ft) over the target; cords lower the rover 7.6 m (25 ft) below the descent stage. NASA gives an altitude trigger, not a clock time: the phase is shown whenever the descent stage is 20 m or less above the ground before touchdown (about 420 s), and its timeline mark sits at the touchdown bound.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Touchdown
raw.note: EDL ends about seven minutes after entry with the rover stationary on the surface; connecting cords are then cut and the descent stage flies away.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

Rock abundance (damaging rocks under the rover): needs a rock-abundance map (thermal differencing or high-resolution imagery), which is not in the global dataset.

raw.caveat: Thresholds are the Mars Science Laboratory (Curiosity) EDL engineering constraints from the JPL MSL Landing Site Selection Users Guide (Feb/Apr 2006, 'working assumptions subject to future review'). They are a published NASA reference point, NOT the final Mars 2020 requirements: the Mars 2020 elevation and latitude limits could not be verified from a NASA page that was fetched and read, so they are omitted. Perseverance used Range Trigger and Terrain-Relative Navigation, which allow terrain that these constraints would reject.
notes: Global DEM slope uses a ~14.8 km baseline, outside the 2-5 km scale of this criterion, so it is not scored.
Slope at 200-500 m length scale: needs sub-kilometre topography (stereo or photoclinometry); the global DEM cannot resolve it.
Slope at 20-40 m length scale: needs metre-scale topography; only available inside Jezero (20 m CTX DEM).
Slope at 5 m length scale: needs HiRISE-class stereo or photoclinometry.
Rock abundance (damaging rocks under the rover): needs a rock-abundance map (thermal differencing or high-resolution imagery), which is not in the global dataset.

narration.text: Loaded the Mars 2020 EDL timeline: 11 phases from entry to touchdown
Ran 10,000 touchdowns: 100% land on ground under 15°
Started the descent at 60× on the timeline: parachute, heat shield, powered descent, sky crane

steps.title: show_edl_timeline
formula: Cruise stage separation: t = -600 s to -600 s
Entry interface and guided entry: t = 0 s to 75 s
Peak heating: t = 75 s to 240 s
Parachute deploy (Range Trigger): t = 240 s to 260 s
Heat shield separation: t = 260 s to 260 s
Radar acquires the ground: t = 260 s to 350 s
Terrain-Relative Navigation: t = 260 s to 350 s
Back shell and parachute separation: t = 350 s to 350 s
Powered descent: t = 350 s to 420 s
Sky crane: t = 420 s to 420 s
Touchdown: t = 420 s to 420 s

raw.label: Cruise stage separation
raw.note: About 10 minutes before entry the cruise stage is shed. Time derived from 'about 10 minutes before entry'.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Entry interface and guided entry
raw.note: Reaches the top of the Martian atmosphere at about 19,500 kph (12,100 mph). Small thrusters on the aeroshell adjust lift for guided entry. Ends at peak heating.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Peak heating
raw.note: Peak heating about 75 s after entry; heat shield surface reaches about 1,300 C (2,370 F). The vehicle then decelerates until the parachute deploys.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Parachute deploy (Range Trigger)
raw.note: About 240 s after entry at about 11 km altitude and about 1,512 kph (940 mph). 21.5 m (70.5 ft) parachute. End time derived: heat shield separates 20 s after deployment.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Heat shield separation
raw.note: 20 s after parachute deployment (derived: 240 + 20). Reveals the radar and the cameras. Radar is active from here to touchdown, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Radar acquires the ground
raw.note: After heat shield separation the landing radar is exposed and starts measuring altitude and velocity, about 7 to 8 km (4 to 5 miles) above the surface, and runs until touchdown. Time bounds: heat shield separation (260 s, derived) to back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Terrain-Relative Navigation
raw.note: Lander Vision System compares camera images with an onboard map at about 4.2 to 2.2 km above the ground, locating the vehicle to about 40 m in under 10 s and able to shift touchdown by up to 600 m (2,000 ft). NASA gives altitudes, not clock times, for this step: it is shown only while the altitude is between 4.2 and 2.2 km; the time bounds are heat shield separation (260 s) and back shell separation (350 s, derived).

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Back shell and parachute separation
raw.note: About 90 s after heat shield separation (derived: 260 + 90), powered descent vehicle about 2.1 km (1.3 miles) above the surface.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Launch Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing (90 s) and Landing Press Kit (2.1 km)

raw.label: Powered descent
raw.note: Begins at about 306 kph (190 mph) and 2.1 km (6,900 ft); slows to about 2.7 kph (1.7 mph) at about 20 m (66 ft). End bound is touchdown at about 420 s ('EDL ends about seven minutes later'); NASA gives the end as an altitude.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Sky crane
raw.note: Starts when the descent stage is 20 m (65 ft) over the target; cords lower the rover 7.6 m (25 ft) below the descent stage. NASA gives an altitude trigger, not a clock time: the phase is shown whenever the descent stage is 20 m or less above the ground before touchdown (about 420 s), and its timeline mark sits at the touchdown bound.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

raw.label: Touchdown
raw.note: EDL ends about seven minutes after entry with the rover stationary on the surface; connecting cords are then cut and the descent stage flies away.

source.title: NASA/JPL Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit, Entry Descent and Landing

steps.title: run_landing_scenario
formula: 10,000 samples, seed 2026, ok = 10,000 (100 %) at or under 15°, p50 slope 0.3°, p95 slope 0.3°
ok fraction = N_ok ÷ N = 10,000 ÷ 10,000 = 100 % (N_ok recovered from the reported percentage)
dispersion = truncated 2-D Gaussian, 3σ = semi-axes 3.85 × 3.3 km, azimuth 0°

result.note: Coarse global DEM: slopes are averaged over kilometres and miss boulders and small craters, so this is an optimistic regional view. Pick a site inside Jezero for 20 m terrain.
result.method: Truncated 2-D Gaussian touchdown dispersion, 3 sigma = ellipse semi-axes; slope limit is the user assumption.

stats.source: Monte-Carlo (ts) on MGS MOLA MEGDR topography, 16 ppd binned to 1/8 degree (heights above the MOLA areoid; file is gzip, 2880x1440 Int16 LE, height = value*scale + offset)

items.label: Max slope on route
items.source: RouteResult.totals.maxSlopeDeg (CTX 20 m DEM, max |edge grade|) vs MissionConstraints.maxSlopeDeg

items.label: Battery remaining at EVA end
items.rule: no-go if remaining < reserve; caution if within 10 points of reserve (ASSUMPTION). Suit power/capacity are assumptions

items.label: EVA duration (walk + dwell)
items.rule: no-go if > EVA limit; caution if > 85% of limit (ASSUMPTION)

items.label: Lowest sun elevation during EVA
items.source: NASA GISS Mars24 (Allison & McEwen 2000) at route vertices; geometric elevation, no refraction

items.label: Longest comms shadow on route
items.source: Line of sight from habitat (mast 10 m) to suit (1.8 m) on the 20 m DEM, Mars curvature included
items.rule: go if no shadow; caution for any shadow; no-go if one stretch > 500 m (ASSUMPTION); antenna heights are assumptions

items.label: Terrain data coverage on route
items.source: CTX DEM 20 m (route planned on 40 m grid); comms/lighting inputs present: comms, lighting
items.rule: no-go if endpoints are nodata/out of bounds, no route exists, or any route vertex has no DEM data; caution if comms or lighting were not evaluated
